translations.text: ... The love of Christ was kindled in his heart.
And he sent a nobleman to bring the bishops of Jerusalem, Antioch, Rome and Alexandria, and he and his mother were baptized together with their palace and camp.
From that time, in the tenth year, Queen Helena went to Jerusalem to search for the crosses.
And in the fifteenth year a certain woman of the royal family fled, [?] whose name was Rhipsime, for whose sake [?] together with her nurse.
And with her was a captive woman, God-fearing, beautiful and comely, who looked like
a child of noble princes. Her name was Nino, and Queen Helena had looked into her story.
She herself had travelled her own road and had worked many healings by the power of Christ. She had come to Greece and was teaching that noblewoman Rhipsime.
Gaiane, Nino and the others with them fled together with Rhipsime, and they came out into the regions of Armenia,
the dwelling places of King Tiridates, and they were martyred there by King Tiridates: forty-nine souls.
But Nino was spared by the providence of God. She set out toward the northern mountains and came to the river Mtkvari. She followed the bank of the river and arrived at Mtskheta,
the great city, the seat of the kings. She stayed there like this for three years, praying to God in secret in a place covered with brambles.
She made a cross out of vine cuttings, set it up there, and prayed before it.
In the fourth year she began to preach and proclaim the law of Christ God, and she said: "For I have found the northern land in great error."
In the sixth year she brought Queen Nana, the king's wife, to faith during her illness.
In the seventh year she brought King Mirian to faith through a miracle worked by Christ. And she quickly built the lower church, of wood, in the Paradise garden.
And that precious pillar, which raised itself up.
They built the church, and the king sent envoys with Nino's letter to Greece, to King Constantine, to ask for priests.
The envoys quickly reached the king.
When the king saw them, he greeted them warmly and kissed them with a smile. And they showed him the letter of the king and of Nino.

When they learned why the envoys had come, they rejoiced with great joy. King Constantine and Queen Helena quickly rose from their thrones and bowed down on their faces before the sovereignty of Christ.
Then they stood up again, raised their hands to heaven, their eyes filled with hot tears, and cried out in a loud voice and said:
"Glory to you, Christ God, who have been pleased to do this." And everyone cried out, "Amen."
Then King Constantine wrote letters with his own hand. He adorned them with much praise and many words of "rejoice," and he named the king his brother, an heir and a fellow sharer in the Kingdom.
In the same way Helena wrote two letters, one for Queen Nana and one for the holy Nino. She too filled them with much praise and many words of "rejoice."
She called Queen Nana blessed. But the blessed Nino Helena lovingly called a queen, her own equal, and equal to the holy apostles. And they sealed those letters.
Then the king sent Bishop John, two priests and one deacon, together with an icon of the Saviour, the wood of life, and other letters from Queen Helena for Nino,
and they set off. When they arrived, King Mirian, Queen Nana and their whole court and camp were baptized in the name of the Holy Trinity.
The bishop and Nino asked for a tree so that they could make a cross.
The carpenters searched and found a tree standing on a rocky hill. Its leaves never fell.
The tree was fragrant and very beautiful, as if clothed with the grace of Christ. The hill where it stood could not be reached because of the rock.
They told the king and the bishop. The king sent his son Rev and the archdeacon [?]. They saw how beautifully the tree stood.
And it was in leaf in the times of [?]. And the archdeacon recited the verse of David, saying:
"This tree is planted by the outflow of the rock, watered by dew from above, and its leaves will not fall forever."
And he commanded the carpenters to cut down that tree.
And they made the form of the precious cross as the archdeacon taught. They made three crosses from the trunk of that tree, as three bodies, and erected them in Mtskheta,
King Mirian set up one cross on the mountain of Maghnari, which is called Tkhoti's, and the other one (!) [?]
near the honourable cross as well. And King Mirian sent to Greece and asked for stonecutters and masons who build with lime.
The king gave them, and they came to Erusheti. They laid the foundation of the church.
And they left there the footboards of the Saviour, our Lord Jesus Christ. Then they came to Manglisi, laid the foundation of a church and left the nails there, and so they came to Mtskheta.
And the king began to build the church of the suburb in stone.
When the king learned that they had first laid foundations in Erusheti and in Manglisi, and had left there those precious boards and nails,
He was filled with sorrow and halted the work he had been pressing ahead with, until he learned from the archbishop that:
"There is with you in this city the garment of Christ, woven in one piece from the top, which those who crucified him divided among themselves,
and these men received the tunic by lot and hid it in this northern city. Their children are here now, and who knows whether they even know the place?
But its time is still to come, when it will appear in glory upon the earth. Likewise the mantle of Elijah is buried here as well."
the king was filled with joy. He at once summoned all the Jews and asked them, "Is it really true?" They confessed the truth and did not deny it.
They said, "Elioz of Mtskheta, Longinoz of Kanisi, Talenav and Misael went from here."
About the tunic, they told how these men had received it by lot, but they denied knowing the place.
Then King Mirian rejoiced when he was told that "long ago the tunic of Christ had come from Jerusalem to Mtskheta."
He gave thanks to God and said, "Blessed are you, Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, for you willed long ago to save us from the devil and from that place of darkness,
when you had these Hebrews bring your garment from the holy city of Jerusalem to this city of foreign peoples. For at the time of your crucifixion our fathers reigned in this city."
After this the king became very zealous. By the will of God, he and his whole dominion went forward in Christianity without turning back.
Then the blessed Queen Nana said, "Blessed is the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,
who sent his holy Word from heaven, by grace, from the mighty throne itself down to the earth.
He was born in the flesh from the seed of David and from the Virgin Mary, holy and spotless, who was pleasing to him. In this way he brought about our salvation.
He enlightened everything under heaven, and above all he saved those who believe in him. For he was born a man and was honoured as the God he is.
He was baptized as a servant of the law, by water and earth [?], but from above the Father and the Holy Spirit bore witness to him and glorified him. He was crucified,
buried, and rose again, and ascended to that same height with the Father. He will come again in fearful glory. To him praise is fitting, with Amen."
When the queen had said this, she went and followed after the blessed Nino.
They took with them the archbishop, the priests and the eristavi (duke). They set off and stopped at Tsobeni.
They summoned all the mountain people: the Chartalians and Pkhovians, and the people of Tsalka. A countless crowd was gathered.
Then the holy and blessed enlightener, the blessed Nino, our mother, stood up and raised her hands to God.
And she called on the holy Mother of God for help. Then she again stretched out her hand toward the people and preached to them the faith of the Son of God.

But when those beast-like people heard the preaching, they turned their heads away from her in hostility. They turned their faces aside and gnashed their teeth at holy Nino, but they were afraid of the queen.
So Nino ordered the eristavi to turn the sword against them a little.
And when he attacked them, they gave themselves up to baptism out of fear and smashed their idols.
And they went to Ertso and stayed in the village of Edomi [?], at Zhaleti, and she baptized the people of Ertso and Tianeti.
When the people of Kvareli heard this, they were frightened and fled over into Tusheti. She brought them back and baptized them.
And Nino went on again to Kakheti. She stayed at Katsareti and baptized the Kaokhni and the Sujni together with their people.
And again she crossed over into Great Kakheti. That blessed woman stayed at the village of Kveli.
And she brought the princes of Kakheti, who were kinsmen of these same kings, baptized them, and [?] their baptism. And at that time,
since she had fallen ill, she set out and reached Kukheti, the village called Bodisi, and could walk no further. The king heard of this, and they were greatly distressed.
And Rev, the king's son, came quickly from the city of Uzharma, with Salome his wife and their daughter, and they stayed by her to tend her.
And the king came, with Queen Nana and Archbishop John, to visit her and to take her to Mtskheta.
But she would not go. Instead she entrusted the priest Jacob to the king and the bishop, so that after her he would hold the see of Mtskheta.
And she gave Salome the letter of Queen Helena, which Helena had written to Nino, honouring her with the titles of apostle and evangelist.
And she gave the wood of life to Queen Nana. And the archbishop celebrated the liturgy.
And he gave the blessed Nino communion in the life-giving blood and body of Christ, and sent her on with provision for eternity.
And she commended her spirit into the hands of the Lord and fell asleep in that blessed sleep, and now she intercedes for us before God. This was in the thirty-
fifth year from her coming to Kartli, the three hundred and thirty-eighth year from the ascension of Christ, and the five thousand eight hundred and thirty-eighth year from the creation of the world.
It was at this time that the falling asleep of our holy, blessed and venerable mother and enlightener, the blessed Nino, took place.
Then both these cities, Mtskheta and Uzharma, and all Kartli were shaken by her death. They came and buried her victory-clad body in her own place, at Bodi,
a village of Kukheti. And how could anyone tell how many tears and how many painful laments the king and the queen poured out?!
And the king did not leave her holy tomb for seven days, he and his whole camp.
And a very great crowd gathered, because many healings were being worked by the grace of Christ.
And blessed are those who keep her commemoration, for they become worthy of great grace.
On the seventh day they celebrated the liturgy over the tomb of that holy woman. And King Mirian and all the people went away, because they were building the Upper Church.
And they finished it in the twentieth year. In the twenty-first year King Mirian died. He was buried in the middle church, by the pillar on the southern side,
while in the pillar on the northern side is a portion of that pillar of light, the living pillar.
In the second year the blessed Queen Nana died. The son of Rev sat as king,
and Bishop John also died. In his place sat the priest whom Nino had wished to have as archbishop.
In the third year from the raising of the venerable cross he made a coffin. He died and was buried with his wife in the lower church.
After him this King Bakur, son of Rev, began the church of Tsilkani and finished it in the thirty-first year.
He died and was also buried in the lower church. His brother sat [as king]. At that time the archbishop was Nerse.
The king brought a canal out to Rustavi and built the church of Nekresi in Kakheti. In his [?] and in his time the Persians came in, and the king withdrew to Khidari.
Then the pitiakhsh of the Persian king, Khuar [?], came to Tbilisi and to Kala as a fortress [?]. Kartli came under his tribute, as did Armenia, Siunik and Vaspurakan.
In his time the nobles built that church of the Holy [?] at Mtskheta and assigned it, with its villages, to the great church. And [?], son of Trdat, reigned.
At that time the archbishop was Elijah. He built the church at Bolnisi. And [?] and the archbishop was Jonah.
The lower church fell down. Jonah passed away and took that living pillar away with him.
After him the nobles built Holy Stephen on the Aragvi.
In those times four archbishops passed away. And [?] the archbishop was Bolnokon [?].
This same man was also eristavi, [appointed] by Barab the pitiakhsh. After him the tenth [king] reigned, and the archbishop was Joel.
Then the Persians carried Vakhtang away. After some time he returned, and the archbishop was Michael.
For some reason Michael struck Gorgasali with his foot, and he drove him from the church.
Then the king was filled with great anger and the colour of his face changed. He was planning many evils to overthrow Christianity,
but God, who wishes no one to be destroyed, sent a good intention into his heart.
He rose, stretched out his hands to God and said: "Glory to you, Christ God! What is this matter?" And he brought woe upon the enemy.
He quickly sent envoys to Greece and asked the emperor and the patriarch for a catholicos. They gave him Catholicos Peter.
With him was Samuel, a monk, holy and worthy. King Vakhtang built the lower church
and installed Catholicos Peter in it. This was in the one hundred and seventieth year from the conversion of Kartli.
By then ten kings and thirteen catholicoi had passed away. From that time the catholicoi began to hold the patriarchate.
The first catholicos was Peter, under King Vakhtang. And [?] reigned, and the catholicos was Samuel.
In his time people settled in the city of Tbilisi and built the church of Holy Mary. And the son of Dachi reigned. And
And [there was] another [?], and the catholicos was Saba, a native of Mtskheta. From then on two others, natives of Mtskheta, held the office of catholicos.
Then John of Zedazeni came from Mesopotamia, he and his twelve disciples, in the two hundredth year after the conversion of Kartli.
And after this [?] reigned, and the catholicos was Makari. And in his time Shushanik was martyred at Tsurtavi. In the time of this Bakur the kingship of Kartli came to an end.
And when the kingship came to an end in Kartli, the Persians grew strong and seized Hereti and Somkhiti. But they took even firmer hold of Kartli.

And they went in among the peoples of the Caucasus and built the gates of Ossetia: one great gate in Ossetia itself, two in Dvaleti, and one at Parchuani in Durdzuketi. And they set those mountaineers there as gate-guards.
And they appointed another man as ruler of the gorge of Tsanareti and placed it under his obedience. And when King Heraclius came, then the Persians were brought low.
And the Persians built the gates of Khazaria and put the Khazars to flight.
Then the Persians ruled over the city, and over Somkhiti, Siunik and Vaspurakan.
And the catholicos was Samuel, and slowly Kartli came together again. And they appointed a great eristavi.
This was the first eristavi, and afterwards he was also curopalates. This eristavi laid the foundation of the Church of the Holy Cross.
And the eristavis built half of the great church of Tbilisi, and the whole people built the other half.
And the catholicos was the fourteenth, Bartholomew. Then Heraclius, king of the Greeks, came down.
And the commander of the fortress called out from the Kala of Tbilisi to King Heraclius to parley [?].
But he stopped where he stood, brought out the book of Daniel, and looked up this saying:
"Then the he-goat of the west shall come and break the horns of the ram of the east."
And Heraclius said: "If this word of the prophet is indeed about me, I will repay you a double reward."
He left the eristavi Jibgho to fight against the Kala, and he himself went to Babylon to make war on King Khosrow.
And within a few days this Jibgho took the Kala and captured the commander of the fortress. He filled him with drachmas, then flayed off his skin and sent it after the king.
King Heraclius came to Babylon, captured King Khosrow, and destroyed Baghdad and Babylon.
And he had the Wood of Life brought out, returned, and by God's command began to rebuild Jerusalem. And he installed Modestus as patriarch.
And he went back again to that same place. And before he arrived in Tbilisi they finished the Sioni, but the Church of the Cross was still unfinished.
This King Heraclius sent heralds to Tbilisi, Mtskheta and Ujarma,
so that all Christians should gather in the churches, and all magi and fire-worshippers should either be baptized or be put to death.
But they did not want to be baptized; they mixed in among the Christians deceitfully, until the king drew the sword against all the pagans.
And rivers of blood were still flowing in the churches. King Heraclius purified the law of Christ and departed.
Stephen ruled as eristavi, and the catholicos was Bartholomew: 15. After that there ruled as eristavi
and in his time three catholicoi succeeded one another: 16 John, 17 Tabor, and Babila, 18.
After this his brother, Stephen also, ruled as eristavi. And the catholicoi were Samuel and Evnon.
And behold, news came that the Hagarenes had seized Baghdad. Because of this they loaded everything belonging to this land onto the mules of the Greeks
and departed. After this the kouropalates ruled as eristavi, and the Youth, and then Arshusha the kouropalates.
And then Varaz-Bakur Apa the patrikios, who converted the Garbanians and taught them Christianity against their will. And then Nerse the Great and his sons:
Philip and Stephen, Adarnase and Guaram the Great, Bakurian and the son of Baldad, and also the sons of Adarnase, Ashot and Gurgen.
And the catholicoi who were from that time [?]: Tavpachag 21, Avlali 22, Ioel 23, Samuel 24, George 25, Kyrion 26, Izibod 27, Te[?] 28, Peter 29.
In all, from Evnos onward there were 45 catholicoi. After this, whoever of the catholicoi succeeded was recorded.

The blessed and most praiseworthy woman Nino, who became for us the evangelist of our hearts and the baptismal font of our souls and bodies, proclaimed to us, like a man, the consubstantiality of the Holy Trinity,
she whom neither her womanly nature held back, nor the weakness of the flesh hindered [?] from travelling those harsh and difficult roads,
nor the multitude of waters, nor being a foreigner, nor ignorance of the language and mixing among foreigners, nor being a foreigner,
but just as when someone has stolen away the beloved child of some woman who loves her children, and for a long time she hears that her beloved is living in a distant land,
and out of her love she is stirred up and spreads out her wings like an eagle,
and in grief she runs and searches and questions all the travellers on the road to that land where her child is reported to be living.
In the same way this holy and blessed woman inquired after this city of ours and sought the salvation of our souls.
As she adorned this northern land, Mtskheta, the seat of great kings, this blessed woman came and convinced everyone of the true confession: the Father,
the Son and the Holy Spirit, baptism, death and resurrection, and after death immortality and life, and the second coming of the Son of God to earth for the life of the righteous,
but vengeance on sinners, which Christ the King of glory will render, for his is the kingdom for ever and ever and beyond, amen.
She was stirred by godly zeal and by longing for the holy Sion catholic church, through which, by Saint Nino, the true light was given to the world so that it might know.
Then Queen Sojia set out to see and venerate holy Sion and the holy evangelist Nino, equal to the apostles.
And on her journey she said fervently: "How did our fathers not understand this true way, of which Roman and Greek merchants tell us, saying:
'Our kings reign in this way, and the churches are like this, and they venerate the cross of Christ'?
And whenever I hear this, I am always drenched with hot tears, as if with blood,
"And now with my own eyes I have seen the light shining forth upon the gentiles. And now what shall I offer to you, holy Zion, but this? First:
I offer myself to you, with my children and my kin, in my faith. And second: the small towns of Baratiani [?]
and the great village of Bodisi I have offered to you." And she no longer got into the chariot. Instead she walked barefoot over the earth and the stones.
And she reached the river Aragvi. The river was in heavy flood, and all her servants turned around and went back.
But the queen walked along the riverbank weeping. As a child longs for its mother's breast, so she longed to see the one she loved.
And the queen was left alone at the river. And Archbishop John and all the people of Mtskheta saw her and said:
"Someone has come with a great company on the far side of the water." And they were holding back [?], so that they might hasten [?] the crossing.
But she, the faithful queen, prayed to God, mounted a horse and went into the water. The water was walled off on this side and that, like a wall, and she came across unharmed.
And the people of the church came out to meet her, and the kings as well, and Salome of Ujarma, the queen.
And everyone came out to meet her. And she came in weeping, as is the custom of believers.
And when she came into the cathedral, the king rose with his palace and camp, and the archbishop with the people.
And they went into the church and held a litany and prayer, for the city was trembling with awe at it.
And they hurried to the church, for Queen Perozhavri was the mother of the eristavi of Kartli [?]. There was [?] and great awe on that day.
And they brought the cross and the prayer from the holy father, the archbishop, and they watched those signs and wonders. At the sight the queen was overcome with awe.
Then the queen brought holy Nino's letter before the king, together with Archbishop John from the village of Bodisi, for he had gone there earlier to be with holy Nino.
And the letter was written thus: "To King Mirian, believer in Christ, united with the holy kings, and in the faith of the Holy Trinity, and in the veneration of his cross.
May God grant you from heaven above, like the cross coming down, an abundance of mercy around the camp and within the palace.
And may the cross of Christ be a boast over all your people, and the Spirit of Christ, of the mouth of the Lord. Amen.
"Behold, I have travelled through the lands of Kartli, all the places of the mountains and the lowlands, and I have completed my preaching of the Gospel.
And I found help from the Lord. Everyone accepted my preaching, and they gave their idols to the fire to be burned.
And they turned from their errors, and received baptism and the veneration of the holy cross, and all have followed the Crucified One.
Because of this it is right for you to rejoice, O king, and to give glory to God, the Creator of all, for in your days God has looked upon this land,
a cleft of the north, whose mountains were covered with the mist of sin and whose plains with the haze of error, so that day was turned into night and light into darkness.
And in it reigned that prince who rules the world, who blew with the spirit of the air and scattered all the souls of men into hell.
The Lord has driven him from the land by the breath of his mouth, and he flees in shame to the places of darkness.
But upon you the midday light has shone, the sun of righteousness, Christ God with his glory. You have seen something new and tasted it, for the Lord is sweet.
Through baptism you have put on Christ, and you rest in the shade beneath his wings.
"As for me, I have now reached the land of Kukheti and the village of Bodi.
And now let Queen Sodzi be remembered, for she has been moved by divine zeal to smash the idols and to convert the people of their eristavate.
She quickly sent to Siunik for her brother and her daughter, and to Vaspurakan for Stereon.
She brought them, and everyone in Bodi was baptized. They came to know God and understood his power, that he himself is the Creator of all creation.
They glorify the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, and they pity their fathers, who died in error.
All of these are hurrying to you there: to that famous city, to the king who has been received by God, and to that temple of God which is full of glory,
which he built for God as an eternal house on earth for the glory of his name. They are coming to see the holy pillar,
which the arm of God lifted up, brought down from heaven and set on its base. They are also coming to worship the holy cross that was raised on the firm hill,
the unshakable rock, and to see the bramble bushes that your eyes saw there. May God lead them from here to you.
"When Queen Sodzi arrives, show her your glory and honour as befits your rank, and accompany her.
Tell them about all the miracles, and show them all the wonderful works and healings,
so that they may know the power of the Son of God and how he helps those who believe. And now, at this same time, send quickly to me the holy archbishop, the good shepherd of the spiritual flocks,
so that he may send me on my way and give me the provision for my soul's journey. For the time has come for my day to end and my sun to set.
It is not that the day and the sun change their order. Rather, night falls on me while the day remains forever. But above all, glorified and blessed is the name of the Holy Trinity. Amen."
Those princes arrived with a large crowd of people at Mtskheta, the great and glorious city,
at the holy place Sion, the house of God. There they saw wonders, miracles and many healings.
Many who had been blind could now see. In the same way, people who had been freed and healed from all kinds of diseases stood and glorified God.
The king, his wife and the whole city were there. Throughout the city there were thunderous shouts of praise and thanks to God, and everyone wept rivers of tears.
Then those foreign princes trembled and did not dare to raise their eyes at all. Instead, with tears, they offered God prayer and supplication as a gift.
Those among them who were sick instantly became alive and well. They glorified the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, and hurried to Nino,
the great light and giver of light, their spiritual mother, for the blessed one was gravely ill and suffering.
Then Astiron, the prince of Vaspurakan, called Abiathar aside in secret and said to him:
"Tell me, beloved: were you not a priest of the Jews, an heir by allotted portion? For it is years since your fathers came here — 503 — and you were [?] of the temples
[and] nowhere has anyone among them heard praise of the Christians. But now, behold, I see you, you and your daughter,
for you have abandoned everything, and by your word you have scattered all your people, and you have felled that beautiful tree and overturned the temple,
and more than anyone you are zealous, a preacher of the service of Christ; you urge and you teach, and I wish to hear the force of your words."
Abiathar answered and said to him: "Come here, you and all the nobles, before the king, and set forth the words according to the facts."
And all gathered before the king. And he began to speak.
Abiathar: "Be informed, you, Prince Astrion, and the princes of the whole land — as the king himself knows — that I am of the kindred of Benjamin, by the law of Moses,
trained from the first and thoroughly in all the books, [as is] all our kindred; and the books of the Jews are very many, and they devote themselves tirelessly to reading them.
For this reason it amazed my mind that all the books forbade looking to any other god, but only to the one God.
And then I was amazed at all this concerning those apostles, after — [?] — Christ, and death for his sake.
And then I was amazed at Stephen and Paul, until I reached the depth of their affairs.
All these books bore witness to this: that the law was to be changed, and that the lawgiver was to come to earth — God —
in the likeness of ordinary men, at the end of times: first birth from a virgin, and baptism with water, crucifixion, burial, the darkening of the heavenly lights,
laying in the tomb, and resurrection on the third day, and ascension into heaven, and coming again in that same flesh to judge all created beings.
All this my own books made known to me truly, and I saw the epistles of Paul, my kinsman.
And I understood his wisdom, and I awaited my deliverance from that former wearisome law of the Jews.
But God used to speak through the mouth of the prophets, and not faith [?]. Now, from that time, they have ceased and fallen silent.
From today back to Christ there are three hundred and thirty-four years, since God has no longer looked upon Israel.
And I was astonished, for there was no teacher or hearer or reader in this land until this day.
When God looked upon this land of Kartli, he sent to it a woman, spotless, quiet in the fear [of God], innocent, holy, God-clothed: holy Nino, our mother.
From her we saw wonders of healings, and awesome signs, and terrible miracles at the raising of this pillar and the setting up of the cross, and again those marvels of her brambles,
until I trembled and became a disciple of her disciple, my daughter.
And I was baptized, I and many of my kindred, and I glorify the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, now and forever."
Prince Astrion marveled greatly at the speech of Abiathar the priest, and he glorified God for all his wonders.
And when the holy and blessed Nino had gone around these regions of Kartli and reached the land of Kukheti,
In the village called Bodbe, she fell ill with a great illness, from which she also died.
Then the kings of the land gathered, together with women and children and a great crowd of many peoples, for they saw Nino's face as the face of an angel,
and they cut off her garment little by little to kiss it, out of faith and by force.
Then all the queens around her begged her,
and bitter tears ran from their eyes because they were being parted from their teacher, who had laboured for the sick and healed everyone without payment.
And the queens Salome of Ujarma and Perozhavr of Siunia spoke to her, and with them all the nobles questioned her and said:
"Queen, tell us how you came to our land to set our souls free, and of what lineage or of which parents you are,
and how you delivered us from the worship of idols and showed us the God who created us, and where your journey began.
Tell us your whole story, queen, as you speak of captivity," O redeemer of captives, blessed one, for behold, we have learned from you
that first there were the prophets of Christ the Son of God, and then the twelve apostles and the other seventy-two, and to us God sent no one
except you." Then Nino began to speak and said: "Daughters of the faith and evangelists of the faith of God,
I see you as like the first women in everything, in faith and in the love of Christ. If you wish to know the ways of me, your poor handmaid, I will tell you everything.
Behold, my soul has come up into my throat, and I will fall asleep forever with the sleep of my mother.
But take materials for writing a book, and write down this poverty of mine and my careless life,
so that your children too may know your faith and how you received me, and these miracles of our God
which you have seen in small part: on the mountains, among them the raising of the pillar, and after that at the spring, and up to my coming here.
The Lord himself knows, and my soul knows, what my eye has seen from heaven down upon the earth."
Then they quickly took writing materials. She began to speak, and they wrote. She told of her parents from before her birth, and said: —
It was in the times when George of Cappadocia was martyred, making a good end for the sake of Christ our God.
In those same days a certain man from Cappadocia, a servant of God of princely rank, went to Rome to serve before the king and to receive a reward.
And in those same days there was a certain nobleman in Kolasta [?], and he had two children, a son and a daughter. His son's name was Juvenal and his daughter's name was Susanna.
Then the nobleman and his wife died, and this brother and sister were left orphans.
They set out and went to Jerusalem, and they put their hope in the Holy Resurrection of all Christians, and they entrusted themselves to it there.
The young man attained the office of devtalaroba [?], and Susanna served Sarah Niaphor of Bethlehem.
And the young man mentioned first came before the king. At that same time the Franks were drawn up against the Romans to fight the king on the plain of Polot Ian [?].
And God gave that Cappadocian youth invincible strength, and he put up a resistance beyond measure against their enemies,
until he turned them back and put them to flight, and he captured the king of the Brangians, and with him eristavis and many princes.
He brought them before the king, the king of the Brangians with them. And the king pronounced a sentence of death upon them.
Then the Brangians began to weep, and they implored Zabilon: "First give us your faith and bring us into the temple of God.
And then let our death come. You are the one who captured us, so you yourself carry out the death sentence on us, and you will be innocent of our blood."

When Zabilon heard this, he told the king and the patriarch what they had said. And he baptized them with Zabilon as their sponsor, and they brought them into the temple of God and gave them communion in the mysteries of God.
And he showed them the glory of the holy apostles. At dawn the Brangians rose, put on burial garments, and went out to the place where men were executed,
that place of blood. They prayed to God over their baptism and communion, and they said:
"In death we are immortal, for the Lord has made us worthy to see such glory and to obtain that inexhaustible provision for the journey,
the body and blood of Christ, the immortal Son of God, who is higher than all heights and deeper than all depths, who is blessed forever.
But woe to our kinsmen who dwell in darkness." And they cried out loudly and eagerly and said:
"Let the swordsman come and take our heads from us, so that we may go quickly before Christ."
When Zabilon saw this, he was moved in heart and mind and wept, for they had stretched out their heads to be slaughtered like sheep, and like lambs [?] they had pity on their children [?],
and Zabilon asked the king to release them to him, and he sent them away fully equipped.
They begged Zabilon to go with them to their land and give the law of Christianity and baptism by water to all their people.
He agreed to what they asked and requested a priest from the patriarch. He obtained an order from the king, and they set out.
When they were one day's journey away, news arrived that the king was returning alive, and all the princes with him.
Then ten eristavates were stirred: Khalaja, Khenebagi, Khimgaragi, Zaqa, Gaza, Zarda, Zarmra, Tamonigoni the royal one, Khogh ghma [?], and Khozaga.
These are the names of the princes who came out to meet them at the great river. And the king divided the people on this side and that side of the water.
They blessed the river, and all the people went down into it. They washed and came up out of it at a single place.
For ten days Zabilon laid his hands on all of them. They set up tents and celebrated the liturgy, and he gave them communion in the mysteries of Christ.
He left priests there and set out the whole order of the Church for them. Then he went back to Rome with great gifts.
But he thought it over and said: "I will go to Jerusalem and give this gift of mine to the service of the holy poor of Jerusalem."
He went to Jerusalem and gave all his possessions to the poor.
That devtelar [?] had been made patriarch. The patriarch and Zabilon became friends. One day he said

Sarah Niaphora said to the patriarch: "This Zabilon is the father and baptizer of the Branji, and a man perfect in wisdom and in the knowledge of God. Give this Susanna of yours to him as his wife." And he did so.
Then they went to their own city, Kolastra. And I was their only child.
These are my parents. My mother raised me in her bosom while she served the poor.
When I was twelve years old, my parents sold what they had and went to Jerusalem. There they gave away to the poor whatever they owned.
Then my father received the sign of the cross from the patriarch and parted from my mother.
He pressed me to his breast and poured his tears on my face like springs of water, and said to me:
"You, my child, are the one to whom alone, by God's will, I became a father.
Now I am leaving you orphaned of me, and I entrust you to the Father in heaven and to God, who nourishes all, who is the father of orphans and the judge of widows.
Do not be afraid, my beloved child!" And he said to me: "Take up the zeal of Mary Magdalene for the love of Christ, and the zeal of the sisters of Lazarus.
If you fear him as they did, he will give you everything you ask of him, whenever you wish."
Then he gave me a kiss and went beyond the Jordan with the men of the wilderness, whose way of life the Lord Jesus Christ knows.
The patriarch gave my mother as a servant to the infirm women. And for two years I served Niaphora, an old Armenian woman from Dvin.
I asked her about the sufferings of Christ, and above all about the crucifixion, the burial, the resurrection and the power of the resurrection, and about his garment,
which they divided at the crucifixion, when they stripped him and cast lots, and about the cross on which the Lord was lifted up, and where the two thieves are,
and about the linen cloths that Joseph of Arimathea wrapped around his holy body, and the napkin that was on his head.
In this way I asked about everything, one thing after another, so that I might know. No one was her equal in knowledge of the way of the law and of the Old and New books.
She began to tell me everything, and said to me: "I see, my child, that your strength is like the strength of a lioness, who roars over every four-footed beast,
or like a female eagle, who climbs higher into the air than the male and takes in the whole earth in the small pupil of her eye.
She sees her food and watches it with fiery eyes, catches sight of it, lets her wings go with a rushing sound and swoops down on it. So will your life be.
And now I will begin and tell you everything. When mortal men saw the immortal God on earth, he had come for the sake of his people,
whom he had brought out of the land of Egypt, and to whom he had given the land on which his eyes always look,
and he came to call the foreign nations and those enslaved to foreign gods, since he wills the salvation of the world that he created.
He began to do good to the Jews: he raised the dead, opened the eyes of the blind and healed all the sick.

When the Jews saw these signs, they were torn apart with envy. They took counsel together and quickly sent soldiers throughout the whole land, so that men from all the tribes would come quickly to Jerusalem. They were saying: "Look, we are perishing."
Then men learned in the law of Moses came from every land, and they rose up as adversaries [?] against the Holy Spirit.
And what he himself willed, they carried out: they crucified him and cast lots over his garment;
and the garment fell to the North, to the citizens of Mtskheta, and they carried it away and laid it away for safekeeping.
And no one is able to see it or to move it until the Lord himself wills it.
But the body of the Lord they buried as an ordinary dead man. And because of the disciples stealing it away, they set guards over the tomb,
but he arose, as he is true God, and neither the sealing of the stone nor the vigilance of the guards could hold him back.
And when it dawned, Pilate and his wife came to the tomb and found the linen cloths lying there,
and Pilate's wife asked for them and went in haste to Pontus, to her own home; she had become a believer in Christ.
And the linen cloths came into the hands of Luke the Evangelist.
But the shroud was not found, just as the body of Christ was not; however, some said concerning Peter that he had managed to take it and that he kept it,
but they did not tell this openly, just as no one knows the place of the crosses either; but whenever the Lord wills, then they will appear.
And I rose and lifted up my hands and gave thanks and blessing to the Lord my God, and I bowed down to my lady for all this account of hers.
And again I asked: "Where is that land of the North, where the garment of our Lord is?"
She told me: "The land of Armenia and of the mountain country is called the North, and it is very much given over to paganism.
For that land is under the rule of the Greeks and the Uzhiks [?]."
In those days a certain woman came from the city of Ephesus to worship at the Holy Resurrection.
And Niaphora asked the woman: "Are Queen Helena and her son and their kingdom still in darkness?"
And the woman said to her: "I am their handmaid and close to their counsel, for the Romans have great eagerness toward Christ, for the faith and for baptism."
And I said to Niaphora: "Send me, and let me go before Queen Helena; perhaps she will let me approach to give an account of Christ before her."
And she informed the patriarch. And the holy father the patriarch, my mother's brother, summoned me,
and he stood me on the step of the altar and laid his holy hands on my shoulders, and he sighed toward heaven and [?] said this:
"O Lord my God, God of the ages, into your hands I commend this orphan, the child of my sister, and I send her out to preach your Godhead,

that she may proclaim the good news of your resurrection wherever her course is pleasing to you. O Christ, be a guide on the way for this servant of yours and give her knowledge of tongues, as you did for the holy apostles."
And he parted me from my mother, and gave me the cross and a blessing, and I set out with that woman.
And when we arrived at that woman's house, there was there a certain woman, [?] of the kings,
named Rhipsime, who longed to go to Jerusalem to be baptized because she confessed Christ.
Then that woman handed me over into the hands of Rhipsime. I had her baptized by the hand of a priest, under my guidance, and with her fifty other souls of her household.
And we went to her house and stayed there two years.
Then God looked upon Greece, and King Constantine and Helena, his mother, believed,
and all the people and their court and camp confessed Christ God with joy, in the year five thousand eight hundred
and forty-one from the beginning of the years, and in the three hundred and eighteenth year from the Ascension of Christ, and all Greece advanced in Christianity.
In the seventh year there was the council at Nicaea, and in the eighth year came our flight from Greece: Queen Rhipsime, and Gaiane her nurse,
fifty souls in all. We set out and came to the regions of Armenia, into the garden of King Tiridates.
They were martyred in that same first month, on a Friday. But I stayed hidden among the thorns of a rose bush, for the rose and the almond were in bloom at that time.
When the souls of those saints were departing, I saw something like a garment coming down from heaven, and a deacon with a stole of light,
and in his hands he held a censer, from which came fragrant smoke that covered the heavens, and with him was a multitude of the hosts of heaven.
And the souls of those saints were joined together with one another.
But when I saw them going before the Lord, and myself left behind in afflictions and distress of many kinds, I cried out aloud:
"Lord, Lord, why do you leave me among asps and vipers?" And I heard a voice that said to me:
"So shall your own taking-away be as well, when this thorn that is around you has all become rose petals and fragrance through you.
But you, arise and go to the east, where the harvest is great but the laborers are few."
For there is no laborer. Then, trembling, I set out and came to Ulepore [?], and I spent the winter there in great hardships.
And in the fourth month I set out over the mountains of Javakheti, to learn in which direction Mtskheta lay,
and on the mountains I came upon a great lake with an outflowing river, which was called Paravani, and I stayed there two days.
I asked the fishermen for food, and I was strengthened by the power of that food, and I gave thanks to God.
And there were shepherds in that same place, and among their flocks they were sounding the night calls [?].
And they were calling on their cursed gods, Armaz and Zaden, and vowing them offerings "when we get back."
Early in the morning I went and asked one of them what village they were from, and he answered me:
"Some of us are from Dabi, some from Sapurtsli, and some are Kinjarians and Rabatians of the great city of Mtskheta, where the gods are gods and the kings reign."
I looked toward the mountains of the north, for even in the days of summer they appeared full of [?]
and harsh snow. And I trembled greatly and said: "Lord, Lord, take my soul from me."
And I took a stone and laid it under my head as a pillow, and I fell asleep at the outflow of that lake.
And in a vision a man came to me, of moderate stature, with hair of half length.
He gave me a sealed letter and said to me: "Rise and take this quickly to Mtskheta, to the king of the pagans."
I began to weep and plead with him, and I said: "Lord, I am a foreign woman and ignorant. How can I go? I do not even know the language. What would I say among foreign peoples?"
Then he opened the letter and gave it to me to read. It was written in the Roman tongue and was sealed with the seal of Jesus.
Ten sayings were written in it, like those on the first tablets of stone.
Wherever this gospel is preached, there too this woman shall be spoken of.
"There is neither male nor female, but you are all one."
"Go and make disciples of all the nations, and baptize them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit."
"A light for revelation to the Gentiles, and for glory to your people Israel."
"Wherever this gospel of the kingdom is preached, in all the world, it shall be told."
"Whoever receives you receives me, and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me."
The Lord loved Mary greatly, because she always listened to his true wisdom.
"Do not be afraid of those who kill your bodies but cannot kill the soul."
Jesus said to Mary Magdalene: "Go, woman, and bring the good news to my brothers."
Wherever you preach in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
When I had read this, I began to pray to God, and I understood that this vision came from heaven.
I lifted my eyes to heaven, blessed the Most High, and asked him for help in my troubles.
And I followed the outflow of that lake and set out on my way.
The water flowed toward the west. I followed that water and met with difficult, harsh roads.
I suffered great hardships on those roads and terrors from wild beasts, until I reached the place where the water began to flow toward the east.
Only then did I find joy. I found some travellers, joined them, and came to the region of Kartli and Urbnisi.
There I saw a countless people who served foreign gods and worshipped fire, stones and wood as gods.
Then my soul was troubled. I went to the shrine of the Jews because of the Hebrew language, and I stayed there one month and studied the character of that land.
Then one day great, countless crowds set out with force from that city. They were going to the royal city of Mtskheta to trade and to pray before Armaz, their accursed god.
I went along with them too, and we arrived at the city of Mtskheta, across on the side of Mogvta, the quarter of the magi, and we stopped on the bridge.
From there I watched the fire-worshipping people in their magianism and error. I wept for their error, and also for my own life as a stranger and for my poverty.
On the next day there arose a terrible, frightening roar from the countless crowds, and the sound of many trumpets.
A countless people came out, like flowers [?] in terror [?], and the sight of them was frightening.
Then another multitude of people came out, beyond counting, with women and children. The king had not yet set out.
As he was coming, people began to flee and to move aside off the road, this way and that. And Queen Nana came out.
Then, slowly, another great crowd of people came out. They decorated all the streets with fine linen, purple cloth, garments of every kind, and many-coloured embroidered cloths.
All the people began to praise the king. Then King Mirian came out, with an appearance too dazzling for the eyes to bear. I asked a Jewish woman what this was.
She told me: "The highest god of the gods, who is Armaz the accursed." And I went to see that Armaz.
Those mountains were filled with banners and people, as if with flowers. I went on ahead to the fortress of Armaz and stood near that idol, in a cleft in the rock.
I saw marvels and a terrible sight. My tongue cannot tell how dreadful it was.
Great fear and trembling came over the kings and all the people. I saw a man of bronze standing there, and on his body he wore a coat of golden mail;
on his head was a golden helmet, and his shoulder-pieces were also of gold. His eyes were like emerald [?] and beryl [?], and in his hand he held a sword,
Like lightning it flashed and turned in his hand, so that whoever touched it was as one who had given himself over to death; and they would say:
"Woe, lest I have fallen short somewhere, or have [?] somewhere according to the word of the Hellenes."
"Or as certain ignorant [?] ones say to the great God of heaven — woe, if he should find any blemish in me and strike me with his sword, of which the whole earth is afraid."
And in fear the king and all his people worshipped him.
At his right stood a man of gold, and his name was Gatsi, and at his left a man of silver, and his name was Gaim; these your fathers held as gods.
From then on I wept bitterly and sighed to the Father in heaven over the errors of the north, the hiding of the light and the grip of darkness.
I looked upon those mighty kings and all his princes, for they had been swallowed alive into hell.
And they called stones and wood their creator, and copper and iron and brass, forged by smiths, their god.
Then I remembered the word which the patriarch Juvenal, the holy father, had commanded me,
namely: "As a full-grown man I send you forth, and you are to reach a foreign land and foreign peoples, dr geveli, ze vl, barkadol [?], which means in Frankish [?]: men who are enemies of God."
Then I lifted up my eyes to heaven and said: "Lord, through the greatness of your power these enemies of yours have lied to you, and your forbearance is in your great long-suffering.
And they do whatever the dust and ashes of the earth devise; yet do not disregard them, for they are your image, for whose sake One of the Trinity became man and saved the whole world.
Look upon these nations also, and be angry with those wicked, invisible spirits, the rulers of the world, the princes of darkness;
but show me, O God of my father and my mother, this your unworthy handmaid and the offspring of your servant,
so that all the ends of the earth may see your salvation, so that this North may rejoice together with the South, and that they may worship you, the only God, through Christ
Jesus our Lord, to whom thanksgiving and glorifying are fitting, now ..."
And behold, in the twinkling of an eye the air was stirred from the west, and fierce winds, and the clouds gave voice with thunder, with a terrible and dreadful sound.
And a swift cloud of dreadful aspect appeared. And the west wind brought a [?] breath of bitterness and stench.
Then every man fled, in the countryside and in the city; and I, seeing their great terror, asked from on high, and time was granted, and everyone hurried into their own dwellings.
Immediately that small cloud of wrath arrived and brought hail, each stone the weight of a litra, upon that place alone, and it shattered those idols,
ground them up and crushed them to powder; and the fierce wind tore down the walls and threw them down the cliff, as your own eyes saw.
And the king said: "Ah, ah, thus: rasatjimeb khaja tabanog ras ol pasa rajd [?]" — another language.
And when the wrath had died down, I came out of the cleft in the rock and found that beryl stone.
I took [?] and came out, across to the western side of that rock, where the old city and fortress had been.
And there stood a beautiful brinji [?] tree, tall and many-branched.

And I went beneath that tree and made for myself the image of the life-giving cross of Christ, and I prayed there six days, at the time when you, the multitude of the city, came out and searched for those gods of yours, upon whom destruction had come.
And you will not find those cursed ones [?]. At that time I was there, for it was the sixth month,
and it was the sixth day of the month, the day on which Emmanuel, on Tabor, showed the image of the Father to the chief of the living and the chief of the dead.
Then this lady of the royal household of mine, Shroshana, came and brought a Greek-speaking woman, and she asked me about my whole journey. And I told her my whole journey and everything I had done.
Then I saw that her eyes were full of tears because I was a stranger in a foreign land, and she pressed me to let her take me away, but I did not want to go.
And on the next day I came down to the city of Mtskheta and made my way to the king's garden.
When I came to the gate of the garden, I found the keeper's small house.
And when I went inside, this woman, Anastoso, was sitting there. When she saw me, she rose and greeted me warmly,
as if she knew me. She washed my feet, anointed me with oil, and brought me bread and wine. And I stayed with her for nine months.
Now this woman was childless, and she and her husband were greatly troubled by it. And one night I saw in a vision a man of shining light come and say to me:
"Go into that garden. Under the fir trees, among the babilo [?], there is a small place prepared as a flower bed. Take earth from that place and give it to her to eat, and she will have a child."
And I did so. And she had many sons and daughters, whom your eyes now see.
In those same days I saw in a vision during my light slumber, two and three times, while I slept on my feet [?]:
the birds of the sky would come and go down into the river, wash themselves, and come into the garden,
and they would pluck at [?] the babilo [?] and feed on all the flowers, and they would call to me tenderly, as if the garden were mine.
They would gather around me, chirping. And they were beautiful to see. I saw this vision many times.
And I told this to my sister Sidonia, daughter of Abiathar. And she said to me: "O captive and deliverer of captives, stranger and yet born here, know now
that through you it has come about, and because of you will be heard, that old story: the deed our fathers committed against the heavenly Man, the shedding of innocent blood,
for which God put the Jews to shame, scattered their kingdom to the ends of heaven, and brought down that holy temple,
and called that foreign people, to give them eternal glory." This she prophesied, and further: "They will spread out their wings for you beneath your wings [?].
Behold, a woman has come here as well, for she will change the whole order of this land."
And she turned to me again and said: "Your vision is like the vision of Jacob, for through you this place will become a paradise forever."
And it came to pass that God looked down in mercy on the forgotten land of the north, the Caucasian highlands and Armenia,
and the whole kingdom, whose mountains were covered with fog and whose plains with the haze of sin. And the land was deprived of the Sun of righteousness,
deprived of the coming and the salvation [?] of Christ, the Son of God, and so it was rightly called by the name "the North."
Not that it lacked this sun of the sky, the one that exists now, which everything under heaven sees and looks upon.
It was called a "shadow" for this reason: because of how many times, years and generations passed from Adam to Noah and to Abraham.

In that time lived Job, who was tested by the Tempter, as Joseph was. Aaron and Moses served as priests and judges, one after another. We know this by hearing it and from the books of the divine Gospels.
Five thousand five hundred years passed before the coming of Christ. From the crucifixion of Christ to the reign of Constantine and the baptism of the Greeks, three hundred and eleven years passed.
Fourteen [years] after that, the true preacher, my lady Nino, was sent to this land of ours, like a star in the darkness,
that is, the morning star, which shines, and after it rises that great ruler of the day, our Illuminator.
This was how we Georgians lived: we turned from the light and lived in darkness. We rejoiced in pleasures and stored up the pleasure of mourning as treasure,
for which no consolation could be found. We served the creature and not the Creator. Instead of the chariots of the cherubim, our fathers worshipped high mountains,
like Ebal and Gerizim, on which there was neither God nor Moses, only cursed idols of stone.
In this land of Kartli there were two mountains, and on them stood two idols, Armaz and Zaden. With their foul-smelling breath they savoured the souls of a thousand first-born children,
whom their parents saw as sacrifices to be offered, forever, not [as] death [?]. There were also other, royal idols, named Gatsi and Gatsa.
One royal child was offered to them: it was burned with fire, and its ashes were scattered on the head of that idol.
After all this I will tell you my father's account. I know it myself from reading books and from my father's telling.
When Herod was reigning, we heard that the Persians had captured Jerusalem and that twelve kings had come.
A letter of mourning came to all the Jews and Georgians: to the residents of Mtskheta, the priests of Bodi,
the scribes of Kodistsqaro and the interpreters of Sopiskani. And so they were all stirred to flee.
A few days later another report came from Jerusalem to the whole land, saying:
"The Persians did not come to conquer. Instead of armour, weapons and provisions, they had as their share [?] yellow gold, myrrh, which quickly heals wounds, and fragrant frankincense."
"Every commander and each of the kings themselves carried one load of these. They were looking for a certain child who had been born, a son of David,
and they found him: a stranger, the son of a stranger woman, a boy born out of season in a place that was no place, as is the custom among outcast people."
"They went to that child, worshipped him and offered him all of this. Then they crossed the mountain and went away."
Then he said: "Now do not be afraid, Jews. I, Herod, searched and did not find the child, or his mother, or those gifts.
But I will send the sword against every child two years old and under, so that he too will perish with them. Now take heart, for it was all an illusion."
Meanwhile thirty years passed. Annas the priest wrote a letter from Jerusalem to our grandfather Ozias:
"The very one for whom the Persian kings came with gifts, that child, has indeed grown up and reached full stature.
He was baptised in the river Jordan by the son of Zechariah.
And all the kin in Jerusalem went out, and your father's mother's brother Elioz was with them.
Behold, the heaven thundered and the earth shook, the mountains trembled, the hills sang, the sea stood still, the waters were stirred up,
the son of Zechariah was afraid and fled, and terror and trembling fell upon all of us. And because of the great number of the people we have kept this matter silent from of old.
And in the fourth year a decree went out from King Herod: "Hear, all you sons of Israel, scattered over all the earth.
Behold the one God and learn the one word of Moses, which he spoke: 'Whoever calls [himself] God on earth, let him be hanged on a tree.'
And again he said: 'Cursed be everyone who is hanged on a tree.'
Behold, a man has arisen whose name is Jesus; of his own accord he calls God his Father and claims that he himself is like God.
Come, all of you, to his death, and let us fulfil the commandment of God and of Moses." And Elioz, my father's mother's brother, went.
He was an old man, and he had a mother from Mtskheta, of the tribe of Eli the priest, and he had one sister.
And his mother pleaded with her son and said to him: "Go, my child, at the king's summons and according to the rule of the law; but as for what they are plotting, do not let your mind join in it.
No, my child, no, for he is the word of the prophets and the parable of the wise, the mystery hidden from the Jews, and light to the gentiles, and life eternal."
And Elioz went, and all the Georgians, and everything was fulfilled that we now know from the Gospels through Nino.
And that garment fell by lot to the Georgian Jews, and Elioz carried it away.
And Elioz's mother, in Mtskheta, heard the sound from Jerusalem when the executioner struck the nail on the cross with the smith's hammer at Golgotha.
She heard it here, and the woman cried out and said: "Farewell, kingdom of the Jews, for you have killed God, who came in the flesh, and the Saviour, and you have become enemies of the Creator.
Woe is me, my wretched self, that I did not die before, so that this sound would not have reached my hearing, nor a little later,
so that I would not have seen it; and behold, now the glory of Israel is about to shine forth upon the gentiles." And with this Elioz's mother died.
And when Elioz brought that tunic of Christ to Mtskheta, to our house, he saw that his mother had died; and then his sister came to meet him,
drenched with tears as if with blood, and she threw her arms around her brother's neck, and quickly took that garment of Jesus from him and pressed it to her breast, and at once her soul departed.
Then there was a great uproar in Mtskheta among the kings and all the people. And King Amazael saw that garment and wanted to take it away.
But for terror of that dead woman, who held it in her hands pressed to her, he was afraid and no longer dared to lay a hand on it.
And Elioz buried his sister, and she holds that garment in her hands, and the place is one that God knows,
and my mother too knows it but does not tell, for it is not fitting for it to be spoken of by anyone now; she said only this:
Let it be enough for Nino's disciples, believers in Christ, that the place is near that cedar which was brought from Lebanon and raised up in Mtskheta.
Besides this, I heard from my father: "There is also another twofold [garment?] [?], clothed with power, here in this same city, in our hands,
…the mantle of Elijah is in the solid stonework of the altar, undiscovered until its time."
And now this robe of Jesus is here, unspoken of until its time. Many times my mother Nino made me press my father
to find out the true place of that robe, but he told us sincerely only this:
"The place is his holy tomb, over which the tongues of angels and of men will not fall silent from singing to God.
That place is above it alone, like the place of Jacob, the ladder that was seen reaching up to heaven, from now until forever. Amen."
I, Sidonia daughter of Abiathar, saw this holy woman Nino at the top of the fortress: first on the high tower of Mtskheta, then beneath the [?]; she sat [?] in the king's gardens,
when the Lord shattered the idols Armaz and Zaden with the terrible wrath of his face, until Queen Nana came to believe. Nana confessed Christ as God and as the Son of God.
Blessed Nino spent six years at this, as she herself says, during which she made us seven women disciples of her faith,
for she performed many healings in secret, until, by God's providence, she began to heal in the palace, starting with Queen Nana.
God showed his power through her in the bramble thicket: by her prayer she healed the queen of a grave sickness that human skill could not cure.
After that, a certain Persian magus, a prince named Khuara, was sick with an evil spirit. He was grievously tormented and near death.
This prince was the brother of Queen Nana's mother. Queen Nana pleaded with our mother Nino,
and our king himself watched this matter with some doubt, for he said to Nino: "O woman, by the power of which god do you perform these healings?
Are you a daughter of Armaz, or a child of Zaden, who came here alive and fell down before them? Mercy be on them too.
They granted you the power of healing so that you might live by it in a foreign land. May they be glorified forever!
Be with us like one of the nurses of our children, honored in this land of ours,
but do not speak that foreign word, and do not wish to speak at all of the erring faith of the Romans. For behold the gods, the great ones,
rulers of the world, spreaders of the sun, givers of rain, who bring forth fruits from the earth, those gods of Kartli, Armaz and Zaden,
searchers out of all that is hidden, and the ancient gods of our fathers, Gatsi and Ga. Let your oath serve to convince people.
Now, if you listen to me and heal this prince, I will make you rich and make you a resident of Mtskheta and a servant of Armaz, even though we saw him destroyed by wind and hail.
Yet that place is unshaken. The cursed Armaz and Etrojano [?], the accursed god of the Chaldeans, are utter enemies of each other:
this one brings the sea against that one, and that one brought this kind of overthrow upon this one, as the rulers of the world are accustomed to do. Let this command be enough for you."
The holy Nino, the baptismal font of Kartli, answered the king and said:
"King, may you live forever in the name of Christ and by the intercession of his mother and of all his saints.
He has sent upon you, and God, the Creator of heaven and earth and the Maker of all created things,
out of his great glory and countless mercy has sent to you, like a spark from a furnace,
one spark of his grace, so that you may understand the height of heaven and the light of the sun, the depth of the sea, and the foundation and breadth of the earth and its base,
and may it be known to you, O king, who clothed the heavens with clouds, so that they thunder with the terrible voice of the air, and the earth is shaken by its force, and thunderbolts run,
and in their track fire blazes up through his wrath; or when the great sea-monster stirs in the seas and the whole earth is shaken, until the firm mountains and the rocks are shattered.
But Jesus will make you fully knowledgeable about all this, who is God in the heavens; and he himself is invisible to all creation except to his Son,
who came forth from him and lived on earth as a man, who accomplished everything for which he had come, and ascended to those same heights with the Father.
He alone has seen the One without beginning; and he alone is on high, and he looks upon the lowly and knows the lofty from afar."
And the saint said to him: "King, your drawing near to God is close at hand. I see that there is a sign in this city:
the desirable robe of the Son of God is here, and some have said that the mantle of Elijah is here too, and many signs are here, which God himself has shown you.
As for me, I healed this prince by the power of Christ my God and by the cross of his passion, just as Christ healed Queen Nana of a great illness.
And what I have told him, he will do, so that he may illumine his soul and bring his people near to God."
Upon this they brought the prince to us, and the saint took the prince and Queen Nana, and we went into the garden, under the fir trees.
And she stood him facing east, [?] him to raise his hands to God, and made him say three times: "I renounce you, devil, and I follow Christ, the Son of God."
And Nino wept with the groaning of her spirit and asked God for help for that man, and we with her, for one day and two nights.
And quickly the evil spirit went out of him, and the prince became a disciple of Nino with all his household and his people,
and he glorified the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, now [and always and forever and ever, amen].
And it happened one day, in summertime, on the 20th of the month of July, on a Saturday, that the king mounted and went out to hunt in the direction of Mukhnari,

He went around the country of Mukhnari and went up into the high forests of the mountains of Tkhoti, so that he might look out over the great fortresses of Aspa, Kaspi and Uplistsikhe, and he went up to the summit of that mountain.
And just at midday the sun grew dark above him, and it became pitch-black night. A very deep darkness covered those regions and places.

Because of that distress and calamity all his people were scattered from one another. The king was left alone, and he wandered over the mountains and through the high forests, frightened and trembling.
And he stopped in one place and gave up hope of staying alive.
But God, who does good, turned his mind from ignorance to understanding and from unknowing to knowledge. He came to his senses, reasoned in his heart and said:
"Look, I see that I have called on Armaz and Zaden with a loud voice, and I have found no relief.
So now let me call on the One whom Nino preaches, the Cross and the Crucified, through hope in whom she works many healings.
Might He not now have the power to save me from this distress? For I am in hell while still alive, and I do not know
whether ruin has come upon the whole earth and light has turned to darkness, or whether this distress is for me alone."
At once he cried out and said: "God of Nino, light up this darkness for me and show me the way to my dwelling, and I will confess Your name.
I will set up the wood of Your cross and worship it. I will build You a house to be Your house and my place of prayer. And I will be obedient to Nino and to the faith of the Romans."
As soon as he had said and spoken these words, day broke and the sun quickly shone out.
Then the king got down from his horse and fell face down on the ground, sighing and weeping.
He rose, stretched out his hands toward the east and said: "You are God over all gods and Lord over all lords,
the God whom Nino preaches. Your name is to be praised by everything created under heaven and on earth.
You saved me from distress, and when I called on your name you quickly turned my darkness into light.
See, I have come to know that you want to save me and bring me close to you. Now I will set up the wood of your cross in this place,
so that your holy name may be glorified by it, and this event and these miracles may be remembered forever." He took careful note of that place, then set off and came away.
When his men saw the light, those who had been scattered and in distress for a long time gathered together again.
The king called out and said to all his people:
"All you people, give glory to the God of Nino, for he is the eternal God, and praise belongs to him alone forever. Amen."
and Queen Nana and the whole city went out to meet the king, for they had heard first that he was lost and then that he had returned in peace.
And there was great joy in the king's palace-camp, for their mourning was turned into joy. And they went out to meet him at Kanjari and Gharta.
But the blessed Nino was standing at evening prayer among the brambles, according to her custom, at the seventh hour of the day.
And when the king came in, the whole city was stirred, and the king cried out with a loud voice:
"Where is that foreign woman, who is my mother, and her God, my savior?"
When the king heard that she was at prayer among the brambles, he bowed down at once, and all his army with him. He leapt down from his horse, fell to the ground and said to the saint:
"Now I know that I have been made worthy to confess the name of your God, who is my deliverer."
The blessed woman taught him and urged him at once to bow down toward the east and to confess rightly Christ, the Son of God.
Then there was a great outcry and weeping among all the people when they saw the king and the queen, for bitter tears were flowing from their eyes.
Then the saint said to the king: "King, listen to me. God has looked upon this land in the days of your reign.
I am a sinful woman, and it is not fitting for me to baptize. Instead, send envoys quickly to Greece, to the rulers Constantine and Helena, together with a letter from me,
so that a bishop and priests may be sent to you, and through them you may be sealed in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit."
On the next day he sent envoys to Greece.
Blessed Nino taught the king the whole true way of God day and night, now and forever and ever, amen.
At that time the king and all the people of Kartli made eager progress in Christianity until the priests arrived.
Then King Mirian said to Nino: "Tell me, blessed one, where I should build a house for God." The saint answered: "Wherever the mind of kings is firm."
The king said: "I love these brambles of yours. That is where I have in mind to build a house for God as a place of prayer for myself.
I will not spare the royal garden, nor the tall firs, nor its fruitful vines,
nor the fragrance of the vines and flowers. There I will build a temple to God as a place of prayer for myself and for the glory of his holy name."
At once they brought timber and began to build the church. They cut down that fir tree and prepared it as a pillar, and they laid the foundation on its roots.
That pillar was awesome to behold. When the time came to raise that great pillar,
the king and his troops struggled with it for a whole week, using every device and human means. They could not raise it, nor even move it from its place.
The king was greatly dismayed and troubled that the pillar could not be raised. Filled with great sorrow, he went to the palace, and he and his people were deeply disheartened.
That night the saint stood beside the pillar. I and twelve women stood behind her and watched all her struggle.
Then the saint lamented and shed tears onto the pillar. When it was midnight, we saw a sight in a night vision, in my sleep:
it was as if these two mountains, Zaden and Armazi, were toppling over and crumbling down in such a way that they dammed the waters of both rivers.
The Kura burst out and was flooding the city. Dreadful sounds of people being taken captive and of people fleeing arose.
Suddenly the sounds stopped, and there was nothing.
Before the cock had crowed, a mighty army fell upon all three gates of the city with terror and broke down the gates.
The city was filled with the Persian army. Terror and shrieking arose, and blood flowed in great quantity.
And a multitude of swordsmen came upon us, and our flesh melted and our soul was worn out. But the holy and blessed one stood unafraid.
And I was weeping for my father, and suddenly I heard them crying out loudly: "The king of kings of the Persians, Khuaran Khuara [?], commands
that all the Jews be saved from the edge of the sword." And those swordsmen had come close all around us, striking and killing.
And a voice was heard, loudly: "King Mirian has been seized!" Then the valiant striver looked down and said:
"Now there is indeed great distress. I thank God. It is clear that this is a sign of their destruction, of the salvation of Kartli, and of the glory of this
place." And she turned to this host around us and said: "Where are the kings of kings of the Persians, Khovar Khoran, Khoran Khova [?]?
Did you come from Sabastan [?]? You came quickly indeed, and with great force, and you shattered this city and struck with the sword.
Now, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, I command the winds and the breezes: carry them off [?] to the farthest places [?]. The one you fled from has come here."
And she stretched out her right hand in the form of a cross, and at once all those demons vanished, and a great stillness came.
And we glorified God and called holy Nino blessed.
And as dawn was breaking, all my sisters fell asleep, but I stayed awake. And the holy one stood with her hands outstretched.
And behold, a handsome young man came near, adorned all over with light and wrapped in a cloak of fire, and he spoke certain words to her, which were a blessing [?].
And holy Nino fell on her face. And the young man put his hand to the pillar, raised it upright, and carried it up to the height of heaven.
And I approached the holy one in amazement and said to her: "My lady, what is this?" But she pressed me down to the ground with her hand, and we began to weep in that terror.
And after a short time, while the other women were also there, behold, we again saw an astonishing vision:
that pillar was coming down from heaven to earth in the form of fire, and it came close to its base, still standing upright.
And it stood about ten cubits above the ground, and very slowly it came down onto its own cut, upon its own fir-tree stump.
At first light the king had risen, heavy-hearted from his sorrows, and he looked toward that garden and toward his church that had been begun, for his mind was fixed on it.
And he saw a light like lightning reaching up to heaven and rising from his garden. And he began to run.
The king came quickly, and the whole multitude of the city with him. They came and saw that wonder:
the pillar, shining with light, was coming down to its place, as if from heaven, and it stood upon its base and was set fast without being touched by human hands.
At that time the city of Mtskheta was filled with fear and joy, and rivers of tears flowed from the eyes of the king, the princes, and all the people.
And they called holy Nino blessed, and on that day many miracles took place.
A Jew who had been blind from birth came and approached the pillar, and at once he received his sight. And they glorified God.
A certain prince, a youth who had been sick for many years, was brought by his mother in faith, and she laid him on a bed before the pillar of light and glory.
And the boy's mother pleaded with the saint, saying to her:
"Look upon my son, my lady, for he is close to death. I know that the God you serve and preach to us is the God of gods."
Then Nino touched the pillar with her hand, laid it on the boy and said to him:
"If you believe in the Son of God, who came in the flesh for the life of the whole world, you will be healed. Then glorify him by whose power you are healed."
And at once the boy got up, as if nothing had ever been wrong with him.
Great fear fell on the king and on all the people, and they gave glory, for sick people with every kind of illness came and were healed,
until the king built a wooden covering around the pillar and hid it from sight.
Even so, the people touched the covering and were healed.
The king immediately began building a church in that garden. He made it splendid with much gold and silver and adorned it with every kind of ornament, so much so
that kings, princes and everyone who saw it could hardly tear themselves away, so great was their love for it.
Then a bishop came from Greece with priests and deacons. The king and all the people began to be baptized, as was written above.
I, Abiathar, was the priest chosen by lot for the priestly service of that year, when this blessed woman came to Mtskheta, the seat of the great kings.
At that same time a letter came to me from the Jews of Rome, Egypt and Babylon, from their priests and scribes. It was written as follows:
"God has split the kingdom of Israel into three parts. Behold, our prophets have fallen silent, because everything the Spirit revealed to them to speak has been fulfilled.
