We have been scattered over the whole earth, and the Romans have taken our land under their rule.
We wept over this with all our hearts to the Most High, but he did not hear us, because we have angered God our Creator.
Now look into the books of Moses, who wrote everything down for us and commanded: 'Whoever calls himself God, hang him on a tree.'
Or perhaps we have sinned in the death of that Nazarene, Jesus. For we know this: in former times, when our fathers sinned against God,
God would wholly forget them and hand them over to harsh rule and captivity. But when they turned back and cried out, his wrath would quickly subside and he would deliver them from their affliction.
We know from the Scriptures that this happened seven times. But now, since they laid hands on that son of a poor stranger woman and killed him,
from that time he has withdrawn his hand from us. He has split our kingdom, separated us from his temple and disregarded our people.
It has been three hundred years since he heard the prayer of any one of us or showed us mercy and comfort.
So now we suspect that this man was from heaven." That is what the letter said.
When I heard this and read the letters, my heart was struck, and I began to ask this woman, Nino, about Christ: who he was, and for what reason God became man.
Then the blessed Nino opened her holy mouth, and her words came forth like springs of water.
And the water of immortality, which had been there from eternity, began to flow. She recited my own books from memory and explained everything to me.
She woke me as if I had been asleep. She enlightened my mind as if it had been dulled. She made me pity my fathers, and she convinced me that the law had been changed.
In the end she made me understand, and through her word I believed in Jesus Christ, the Son of God, and in his passion and his resurrection,
and also in his second coming in glory. I believed that he truly is the hope of the Gentiles.
At that time my daughter and I were found worthy of the sprinkling that cleanses sins, the water of the baptismal font. David longed for it but was not found worthy of it.
And I myself also heard the voice of the companies of singers, which that same David longed for.
And now I have been found worthy of the true body and blood of the Lamb of God, offered for the sins of the world. Its taste is sweet.
And with my own eyes I saw many miracles performed by Nino in Mtskheta.
In those days a letter from the holy patriarch arrived from Rome. It was addressed to Nino, and it came before the king and all the people.
And they sent bishops and deacons to offer praise and to give a blessing. They also came to receive the gift of this blessed woman's prayer and to share in her grace.
And they had a letter for Nino from the king of the Franks, because the Franks had been baptized by Nino's father.
News of all these miracles had reached them from Jerusalem, Rome and Constantinople. They had heard that the Sun of righteousness, Christ, had spread his light over that northern land.
That is why the letter had been written: so that they too might learn of the miracles that those who came would see.
They left full of joy. They took letters with them, and they glorified God.
Written down.
And it happened that they cut down that tree to make the cross. A hundred men carried it with its branches and leaves still on it. When they brought it into the city,
a great crowd of people gathered around it, because they delighted in how green and full of leaves it was.
It was the beginning of spring, and every other tree was still bare. But this tree's leaves had not withered and it was fragrant. The tree was beautiful to see.
And they set the tree upright on its roots by the door of the church, on the south side. A gentle breeze blew from the waters and stirred the tree's leaves and branches.
Its appearance was beautiful and lovely, like the aloe tree that we know only from what we have heard.
The tree, called Kilmor [?], was cut down on Friday, the 25th of March.
And the tree stood for thirty-seven days, and the colour of its leaves did not change. It was as if it were still standing on its own roots.
Then on the first of the month of May they made three crosses. On the seventh day they set them up, with the laying on of the king's hands and with the eager support of all the people.
And those crosses were in the church. And every night at dusk the whole population of the city saw
a cross of fire, crowned with stars, come down from heaven. It would stand above the church until dawn.
And at dawn, two stars would come out of it; one would go off to the east and one to the west.
And that sovereign thing, which is the cross of Christ God, would likewise rise slowly and go to the far side of the Aragvi,
and would stop on the rocky hill, on its upper side, near the spring that the tears of Saint Nino had made spring up, and then it would rise up to heaven.
And so all the people saw God's saving power many times.
Then the king began to beg everyone to tell him about all these things: "My lady, what is this sign that shines out so clearly?
For at night, in a terrifying vision and in a light the eyes cannot bear to look at, we see the sign of the cross coming down from heaven to earth, and this pillar of light
standing over it all night long. Then at dawn it moves slowly back onto that hill and rises again from the earth up to heaven. Or is it a crown adorned with stars?
And what are those sparks that go off to the east and to the west? What is all this? Tell us, my lady."
And Saint Nino said to him: "Yes, king," she says, "do not search for what cannot be searched out, and do not test what cannot be tested, for His works are beyond understanding.
Now know this: God has looked upon you and honored you above all the kings of the earth.
Rejoice and be glad! For He has now sent you the cross on which He stretched out His hands of His own will, to deliver you from all the snares of the enemy.
So now quickly send men onto the high mountains, from the east to the west, as far as your kingdom reaches.
And when those stars shine out, let them mark the place, and in that place let these two crosses of Christ be set up."
Then the king did so and had the mountaintops watched one after another.
That day was Friday, and as Saturday was dawning the same sign appeared, and everything happened just as it always did.
And the next day the men from the west came, the ones who had stood on the summits of Kvabtatavi.
They told the king how that star had come out, risen up, and reached the mountains of Tkhoti, at the pass of Kaspi, and how it had stopped at one place and slowly vanished.
Likewise men came from the mountain of Kukheti and said: "We saw a star coming this way, and it stopped at our village of Bodi, in the land of Kukheti."
Then the blessed Nino ordered the bishop and a large crowd of people to go and take those two crosses and set them up where God had revealed [the places].
"Set one at Tkhoti, and give the other to Queen Salome, the handmaid of Christ, so that she may set it up in the city of Ujarma,
so that the village of Bodi may not become a rival to the royal seat, for a very large number of people live there.
We will see to the village of Bodi ourselves, that place pleasing to God." And I did as Nino commanded us.
And we raised up with human hands this precious cross of the Savior, which had been revealed by a heavenly sign.
And the king went out with all his princes and all the people of Kartli, together with women and children.
And we came to the foot of that hill, by the spring, and spent the night there and prayed to God."
And holy Nino mingled the spring with her tears, and healings and many miracles took place.
On the next day we went up onto that rock, and the saint also came onto that hill and fell down upon the stones,
and she wept bitterly, and so did the kings and the princes and the whole multitude of the people, with the women and the infant children.
The weeping and wailing rose up to heaven, until even the mountains cried out together with them. And great fear came upon every soul.
And trembling, they glorified the divinity of Christ and his precious cross.
Blessed Nino laid her hand on one stone and said to the archbishop:
"Come, it is fitting for you to make the sign of the cross on this stone." And in that place they set up that glorious cross.
And the saint and the kings and the princes and that whole multitude of countless peoples bowed down and worshipped the holy cross,
and they confessed the Crucified One as truly the Son of the living God, and the Trinity as glorified, one in essence. Amen.
And the queen and the other noble women never left the church of the living and luminous Pillar,
for they saw the signs and the indescribable healings of that precious cross.
Then holy Nino left the city of Mtskheta and went to the mountain people, to preach to those men who were like beasts and to smash their idols.
In Mtskheta she left the priest Abiathar the Jew, who was a second Paul. He never ceased preaching Christ and his glory,
until the Jews began to flee, for the Jews were pressing the king not to disturb that sanctuary,
while the new grace had not yet appeared in this land, the name of the Eternal One was in that temple.
And the king [?] in his days, and the kindred of Elioz served in it as priests over the Jews.
And it came to pass at the time when you remembered, O Lord, the land of Kartli, darkened by sin and full of error through the service of demons,
and we were like sheep for the slaughter. For I am the thirty-sixth king from the time our fathers came here down to my own days.
Fire consumed their children as sacrifices to the idols, and the innocent people of this land, whose children, like spotless lambs,
our fathers offered up and took upon themselves by force, so as to please the idols, and above all those two accursed ones, Armaz and Zaden,
whose stones they have rotted with the blood of infants. Those mountains deserve to be burned up with fire from the Lord.
But when this our mother, holy Nino, came to this land, at first as a captive and a stranger, as a pilgrim and without help, as one speechless and [?] (perhaps "unheard"),
through whom that captive has now become a queen to me, and that foreign and helpless woman a refuge for all, and that speechless one a mighty preacher and one who knows my hidden things,
this blessed one lit the lamp of light in my heart, and in the very middle of the night she showed me, shining brightly, the Sun of righteousness,
Christ God, whose light shall never fail, forever and ever. Amen.
And she became our teacher, and she won us for Christ God through baptism and through the veneration of the Cross.
She gave us the new law of life and of joy, and made us worthy to taste the mysteries of heaven.
And I became obedient to the commands she taught me.
And I built my church as a place of prayer for myself in the garden of our fathers the kings, and in it this pillar of light,
which I could not raise with all human strength and knowledge; but the Most High sent one of his servants, and at his bidding it rose from the earth to heaven.
Your own eyes saw this wonder of it, and after it the further miracles and healings which it performs day by day.
And when holy Nino told us to set up a cross, I sent out carpenters, and they searched for a tree until they found one standing alone on a rock,
which no human hand had come near. But we knew of the miracle of that tree by hearsay from hunters: when an arrow struck a deer,
it would quickly flee to the foot of the hill on which that tree stood, and quickly eat of the seed fallen from that tree, and escape death.
They told me this, and I was amazed. For this reason I cut down that tree and made three crosses.
One of them, whose sign came from heaven, whose glory no human tongue is able to tell,
for hosts of angels would come down upon that place, upon Golgotha, where I set up the cross of my Saviour,
and would sing without ceasing, with worship, and they would sing praises of "Holy in essence" so that all could hear.
And one I set up at the place where I saw the vision from the Lord, on Mount Tkhoti, and one in the city of Ujarma, which my daughter-in-law Salome took away.
And I built a church over Nino's bramble bushes. I did not cut out even one leaf, but enclosed them all around, leaving them unharmed [?],
for I had seen many miracles and great healings that Nino worked there.
And I built the upper church for myself and for the multitude of the people, because the lower church was called "the Holy of Holies."
And we did not dare to open its doors at all except on Sundays. The chief priest would go in, along with the priests who sing in it,
for everyone was in great fear of that living pillar, because everyone looked on that pillar as the power of God.
Nor did I dare to dig earth in front of it for a grave for my body, so that I might be buried before it, for I was afraid, being nothing but a doer of sin.
And I prepared a grave for myself in the upper church, so that I might keep out of its sight, and might receive its mercy at the general resurrection.
And when all the good things of God had been fulfilled for me, and I was full of joy and gave thanks to God,
and I resolved in my mind to commend my soul to my mother, holy Nino,
behold, sudden sorrow and great mourning came upon us and upon all the people of Kartli, for we were orphaned of our mother, our enlightener.
Then she commended her spotless soul into the hands of the Lord, her Creator.
Truly she fulfilled every commandment of her Lord and the teaching of the holy father, her mother's brother, and she left us orphans,
like newborn infants. I trembled, and so did the whole northern land, at her departure, for the sun had only just risen and its light had spread.
Behold, the winter cloud has hidden it from us. But the holy one is wholly in the light, and she enlightens all who call upon her holy name.
And I firmly resolved in my heart to move her holy relics to Mtskheta and carry them before the Pillar of Light.
Behold a fearful and terrifying thing: I found no way to carry out the wish of my heart.
The feet of our horses could not move forward, and two hundred men could not move the bier on which she lay at rest.
And many who were afflicted were healed, and people hurried from every side to touch her holy body.
Then on the third day, with great difficulty, we buried her body, wholly clothed in her ascetic struggle, with great honour and glory at Bodbe, in the village of Kokheti.
And I mourned over her holy grave for seven days together with my kingdom.
And over it I built a very great church and adorned it with every kind of adornment.
And I gave it many villages and estates as offerings. And now, through her intercession, I have hope from Christ the Son of God. In the mighty faith of the Father and the Son
and the life-giving Spirit I fall asleep, and I await the last resurrection. I commend my soul to all of you who sing praises, through the Lord. Amen.
"Behold, I am going back to where I came from. And you, Nana, if God grants you a time of life after me,
divide my kingdom in two and take one part to Bodbe, to the tomb of Saint Nino, so that the length of time and its changes may never shake that place, and it may stand unmoved forever and ever."
And likewise he begged the archbishop to establish her glory, which is worthy of honour, "so that I too may be made worthy of eternal life."
And he taught his son, saying: "Behold, my child, our darkness has been changed into light, and our sorrow into joy forever,
for we who were nothing have been changed into being by the power of Christ God, who from the abyss,
